record.paper_title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems
record.original_question: How do anonymity protocols for peer-to-peer systems degrade under active attack, especially when intermediate proxy nodes may collude, and what protocol designs can better preserve anonymity in those adversarial settings?

evidence.quote: The degradation of anonymity protocols under attacks has been studied in [44], and this study suggests that further work is necessary in this area.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a peer-to-peer network modeled as a graph G=(V,E) whose nodes are participants and whose edges represent communication links. An anonymity protocol on G is a randomized routing scheme in which a message originating at a source s in V is forwarded to a destination d in V through a sequence of intermediate proxy nodes, with the goal that no observer can determine the identity of the sender (sender anonymity), the receiver (receiver anonymity), or the linkage between them (relationship anonymity). Formalize an adversary model in which a subset C of the proxy nodes is actively malicious and colluding: the adversary controls the nodes in C, can observe all traffic passing through them, can drop, delay, replay, or inject messages, and can share all observations among the nodes in C. Quantify anonymity by a measure such as the entropy of the posterior distribution that the adversary assigns to the identity of the sender (or to the sender–receiver pair) given its observations, or by the probability that the adversary correctly identifies the sender.

(a) Give tight upper and lower bounds, as a function of |C|/|V|, of the network topology, and of the protocol parameters (e.g., path length, mixing strategy, cover-traffic rate), on the anonymity provided by representative anonymity protocols for peer-to-peer systems (such as Crowds-style probabilistic forwarding, onion-routing/Tor-like layered encryption, and DC-net-based broadcast schemes) under the above active colluding-proxy adversary.

(b) Determine whether there exists a protocol that, under such active colluding adversaries controlling a constant fraction of proxy nodes, preserves a non-trivial level of sender, receiver, and relationship anonymity (e.g., adversary success probability bounded away from 1 by a constant, or anonymity-set size growing with |V|), and exhibit such a protocol or prove its impossibility.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, as posed at the level of a research direction (degradation of P2P anonymity protocols under active colluding-proxy attacks and the design of better-resistant protocols), has been the subject of extensive subsequent research (e.g., predecessor-attack analyses of Crowds, traffic-analysis and Sybil/eclipse attacks on Tor and onion-routing, and provable-anonymity frameworks). However, no single resolution exists; impossibility results show fundamental limits against strong active adversaries while practical protocols continue to be proposed and broken. The status of the broad question is therefore best described as unknown / ongoing.
